title: Predicting food crises using news streams
target: IPC phase and crisis outbreak (FEWS NET)
data_sources: Factiva news 11.2M articles; ACLED; prices; climate; geography
label_availability: Measured 3-4 times a year in every district
predictors: 167 news features; conflict; prices; rainfall; NDVI; lagged IPC at three scales
news_integration: Share of articles per district-month mentioning a causal food-crisis phrase; Granger filter on an early period
reported_results: 3-month RMSE: experts .189; traditional .149; news .099; both .082. Recall at 80% precision 1145/1432/1677 of 1852
limitations: English only; weaker where coverage is thin; no persistence baseline reported; removing top sources raised RMSE up to 39%
applicability_to_aipheed: Template for feature construction and hybrid test. Gain rests on about 1000 districts measured repeatedly, which aiPHeed lacks

title: Machine learning can guide food security efforts when primary data are not available
authors: Martini; Bracci; Riches; Jaiswal et al.
scope: Multi-country; sub-national assessments in 78 countries (FCS) and 41 (rCSI) per the preprint
target: Prevalence of insufficient food consumption; crisis coping
data_sources: WFP surveys; ACLED; prices; NDVI; rainfall
label_availability: Surveys where available; model fills unsurveyed areas
validation: Holds out areas and countries per the preprint
reported_results: Preprint reports up to 78% of variation explained
limitations: Nowcast only; forecasting is a separate WFP product
applicability_to_aipheed: Supports borrowing labels across places. Does not supply a time signal

title: On the forecastability of food insecurity
data_sources: WFP near-daily phone surveys; conflict; weather; economy
reported_results: Beats last value; skill rises with number of past observations
limitations: Depends on dense monitoring that CALABARZON lacks
applicability_to_aipheed: Number of observations drives skill; directly explains aiPHeed's ceiling

title: Forecasting trends in food security with real time data
authors: Herteux; Rath; Martini; Baha; Koupparis; Lauzana; Piovani
model: ARIMA; XGBoost; LSTM; CNN; reservoir computing
validation: RMSE comparison; split n/r in abstract
reported_results: Reservoir computing best, resists overfitting on limited data
applicability_to_aipheed: Limited relevance: needs daily labels

title: Forecasting transitions in the state of food security with machine learning using transferable features
authors: Westerveld; van den Homberg; Nobre; van den Berg et al.
data_sources: IPC; open climate, market, conflict data
predictors: 130 variables, food security history and soil moisture influential
reported_results: F1 macro .51 at 3 months, .61 at 7 months
limitations: Ethiopia only; F1 modest even with rich labels
applicability_to_aipheed: Shows that predicting change is far harder than predicting status

title: Predicting Food-Security Crises in the Horn of Africa Using Machine Learning
authors: Busker; van den Hurk; de Moel; van den Homberg et al.
predictors: Climate; market; conflict; socio-economic; lagged IPC
reported_results: Dynamics captured to about 3 months, R2 above .6; similar to FEWS NET in pastoral zones, weaker in crop zones
applicability_to_aipheed: Evidence that reliable horizon is short and empirically found

title: A data-driven approach improves food insecurity crisis prediction
reported_results: 83-99% of the most food-insecure clusters identified against 0-10% for the prevailing approach
applicability_to_aipheed: Closest design to aiPHeed: survey round to next survey round
